title: gRNAde — RNA sequence design for a target structure
description: Design candidate RNA sequences for a target 3D structure (inverse folding). Outputs are candidates for the supplied backbone — a successful run does not validate folding or biological function.
citation: Joshi et al., gRNAde: Geometric Deep Learning for 3D RNA inverse design. https://github.com/chaitjo/geometric-rna-design

fields.name: structure
fields.label: Input structure
fields.help: One PDB file with a single RNA chain.

fields.name: chain
fields.label: RNA chain
fields.help: Auto-detected if the structure has a single RNA chain.

example_summary: A real 12-nucleotide RNA hairpin (PDB 1ZIH, chain A, sequence GGGCGCAAGCCU), bundled so you can run a genuine design without hunting for a structure.
example_details: This is a real RNA structure: the first NMR model of RCSB PDB entry 1ZIH — a 12-nucleotide single-chain hairpin (chain A, sequence GGGCGCAAGCCU) with full backbone atoms, small enough to run quickly. gRNAde's job is 'inverse folding' — given this 3D backbone, propose RNA sequences predicted to fold into it. The designs are candidates for the supplied backbone; a successful run validates neither folding nor biological function. On the fake backend (no GPU) all sequences are deterministic placeholders; real gRNAde designs come from the Runpod endpoint whose image bakes the checkpoint (see deploy-docs/GRNADE_DEPLOY.md). Swap in your own PDB (one RNA chain) to design for a different target.
notes: Real runner landed (worker/run_grnade.py: checkpoint-gated real path via upstream's programmatic API; raises on failure, fails loudly without the checkpoint). source_commit is verified from GitHub (gRNAde v1.0 release 2025-12-15) but build-unverified. checkpoint_digest is the sha256 of gRNAde_drop3d@0.75_maxlen@500.h5 (HF chaitjo/gRNAde rev 91491fc71584bf37fee8297781edf7df07b1d349, 8,726,092 bytes), pinned 2026-11-07; worker_image_digest, max_sequence_length and structure max_bytes stay provisional until a real Runpod smoke run. Code license MIT; the gRNAde checkpoint is MIT, but the HF repo also bundles rhofold/ribonanzanet weights under their own LICENSE files (not baked into this image). Adapter exposes raw sampled designs (temperature 0.1) and deliberately omits upstream's RibonanzaNet scoring/filtering loop; upstream-parity is checked against gRNAde.sample, not design.py's filtered CSV.
